text:
maria: Hey infra team — need a quota push for a new customer pilot. Account 987654321012, region ap-southeast-6 (new AZs). Asking for p5 instances (p5.48xlarge) x6, g5.48xlarge x4, and ENI/IP ceiling bump for the account. Current subnet plan is /26 per AZ but pilot wants denser hosts; can we get guidance on expected ENI counts and whether we should request /25s?

kev: Thanks Maria. Can you paste the account ARN and a one-line justification we can put in the AWS support case? Also which AZs are we targeting (ap-southeast-6a/b/c)?

maria: Account ARN: arn:aws:iam::987654321012:root. Justification: "Pilot for enterprise customer with latency-sensitive inference workload; reserved capacity for 3-week pilot with expected sustained 200 tokens/s aggregate." Target AZs: ap-southeast-6a, ap-southeast-6b.

raj: fyi — for p5/g5, AWS usually requires both accelerator entitlement and ENI/IPv4 ceilings. I'd request: Accelerators: p5.48xlarge: 6, g5.48xlarge: 4. ENIs: increase elastic network interfaces to 800 (account-level ceiling) and private IPv4 addresses to 3200. Also request increased Elastic IPs if NAT per-AZ public egress is needed.

raj: Copy/paste support ticket template below (use as-case description):

```
Account ID: 987654321012
Region: ap-southeast-6 (ap-southeast-6a/b)
Requested increases:
 - EC2 Accelerators (p5.48xlarge): +6
 - EC2 Accelerators (g5.48xlarge): +4
 - Elastic Network Interfaces (ENI): increase to 800
 - Private IPv4 address limit: increase to 3200
 - Elastic IP quota: increase to 50 (if possible)
Reason: Reserved capacity for enterprise pilot. Workload: real-time LLM inference (low-latency), will run ~24/7 for 3 weeks. We need predictable instance availability and enough ENIs/IPs for dense node packing and multi-tenant NAT.
Business contact: Maria Lopez, maria@redwood.ai
Estimated start date: 2026-04-05
```

sophie: Quick networking note — if we're packing many GPUs per VPC, per-subnet CIDR matters. /26 will constrain ENI density if we attach multiple ENIs per instance for monitoring/VPC endpoints. I'd prefer requesting /24 per AZ or at least /25. Also consider using AWS-provided prefix delegation for NAT gateways to reduce EIP usage.

maria: Good call. For pilot we can take /25 per AZ. I've added that to the ticket text.

infra-ops: Filing the quota case now. Using service code ec2 and quotas page. Adding justification and tagging with #pilot-priority. Will request a direct lambda to account manager for faster turnaround.

aws-quotas-bot: Automated reply — Support case created: case-id 1122334455. Estimated initial response within 6-12 hours. Request type: QuotaIncrease (EC2 Accelerators, ENI, IPv4, EIP).

kev: Nice. @raj @sophie — once they reply with accelerators approved we should prebook capacity via Spot/On-Demand hybrid reserve? Also costs: p5.48x and g5.48x are expensive — what's the rough monthly delta for this pilot?

raj: Back-of-envelope: p5.48x ~ $32/hr, g5.48x ~ $24/hr (on-demand), so daily ~ (6*32 + 4*24)*24 = (192 + 96)*24 = 288*24 = $6,912/day -> roughly $207k/month for 30 days if fully on-demand. We'll do reserved short-term or Savings Plan plus burst capacity to reduce that. Recommend budgeting $60-80k for the 3-week pilot with aggressive batching and autosuspend.

maria: Noted, I'll relay to sales/finance. For now priority is quota approval.

infra-ops: AWS replied (case 1122334455): they asked for topology details and whether instances will use ENI trunking. I attached the subnet sizes and confirmed we'll use IPv4 only for pilot. Waiting on quota entitlement approval.

maria: Thanks. If they ask for a PO or committed spend, I can sign a short commitment under pilot terms.

kev: Cool. Keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

sophie: Also added a short note to our infra playbook about requesting larger CIDRs for dense GPU clusters — saving this thread as reference.

maria: Awesome, thank you all.

infra-ops: Case updated: AWS provisionally approved ENI and IPv4 raises, accelerator entitlement under review. Will ping if they need additional justification.

maria: Great — fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:
